name: paddle_shift_market
title: Paddle shifter behaviour: Europe or North America
intent: Choose whether the steering-wheel paddles behave as on a European or a North American car. This is a configuration (PROXI) change in the Body computer, not a reset.
status_note: steps is EMPTY on purpose: no bytes are invented. The only public figures are single-source forum posts (see public_values), recorded for reference and never to be written. Fill steps only from the manufacturer's documented procedure and cite it in source.

session.note: bus and bitrate are the confirmed CAN-C values; the diagnostic session comes with the manufacturer's documented steps

read_back.label: No read method for the current value is known. The manufacturer must supply one so a before and after can be proven.

preconditions.label: unknown until documented. The gap study names battery support and engine off as items the manufacturer must confirm (docs/project/ALFAOBD_GAP.md section 3).

postconditions.label: unknown until documented
postconditions.note: PROXI alignment is required afterwards (see follow_up)

verification_rule: Unknown until the manufacturer documents a read method. Nothing is claimed.

options.label: Europe
options.meaning: The [+] paddle shifts from Park or Reverse into Drive, and [-] together with [+] shifts to Neutral.
options.source: https://giuliatech.com/t/multiecuscan-mes-popular-settings-compilation/80 (repeats a giuliaforums.com post of 2024-04-05 by FizzGiGG; single source, forum, not manufacturer documentation)

options.label: North America
options.meaning: The paddles do not give the European shift into Drive or Neutral. The source describes only the European behaviour; the North American behaviour is its absence, as stated there, and is not described further.
options.source: https://giuliatech.com/t/multiecuscan-mes-popular-settings-compilation/80 (single forum source; the North American value is given there as the alternative setting)

follow_up: PROXI alignment required after the change (source: docs/project/ALFAOBD_GAP.md section 3, citing https://giuliatech.com/t/multiecuscan-mes-popular-settings-compilation/80)

risks.risk: Neighbouring bits control other settings; the same forum author warns of this.

A PROXI mismatch is the larger risk: the BCM holds the configuration and downstream modules compare to it. CUORE's own notes record a TCM P1500 limp-in on mismatch and an alignment failure on a wrong or silent module. Owners also report alignment timing out on a Bluetooth adapter (one user).

needs_from_manufacturer: The documented configuration (PROXI) data map for the 952 and 949: the identifier or block, option names, allowed values, and which bits are paddle behaviour per market and model year.
A read method for the current value, so a before and after can be proven.
The alignment procedure: preconditions (battery support, engine off), module roster rules, failure handling, and the restore path for a backed-up configuration.
Which trims carry paddles, and the market codes that decide the default.
Written authority for CUORE to write it, then the existing path: dry run, gate, typed consent, read-back, audit.

public_values.note: single-source forum figures, recorded for reference only, never to be written
public_values.detail: Body computer, CAN Setup, byte 156, bits 4 and 5. Europe is xx00xxxx, North America is xx01xxxx. Source: https://giuliatech.com/t/multiecuscan-mes-popular-settings-compilation/80 (repeating a giuliaforums.com post of 2024-04-05 by FizzGiGG). Another post says a logic 0 enables EU control: https://www.giuliaforums.com/threads/alfaobd-and-multiscanecu-some-alfaobd-settings-i-was-surprised-by.55899/. Byte 156 is a vendor-tool index, not a published DID, so it may differ by build year and trim (inference in docs/project/ALFAOBD_GAP.md section 3).
